title: I made a VR rhythm game where any YouTube song becomes a playable chart
author: These-Station-9021
selftext:
Hi! I'm the solo dev of BeatCloud, a rhythm game for Windows PC.



Pick a song and it analyzes the audio and builds a chart automatically. You can play in VR, or with a mouse and keyboard.

There are 5 modes (Saber, Drum, Guns, Boxing, Dance), and some charts even switch modes mid-song. There's also a chart editor, so you can make your own charts and share them, plus online rankings.



It's in Early Access now and I'd love feedback.

Which mode would you want to try first, and what songs would you throw at it?



Store page: [https://store.epicgames.com/p/beatcloud-253c22](https://store.epicgames.com/p/beatcloud-253c22)

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/These-Station-9021 please add a bit about how you used AI and what the development process looked like. A mention that AI was involved isn't enough. It needs dev details. Rule 4 exists so promotional posts contribute to the conversation about making games. We want to avoid the sub getting drowned in low effort promotion. If this isn't updated, it may be removed.

replies.author: These-Station-9021
replies.body:
Tools

\- Code: Unity 6 (C#, OpenXR). I use an AI coding agent (Claude Code) to write and edit the C# code, fix bugs, run compile checks and builds, and translate the UI into 9 languages.

\- Server: the ranking, chart sharing, replays and search relay run on Cloudflare Workers (D1 + R2). That backend was also written with the AI agent.

\- In-game AI (optional): Gemini generates stage effects and AI charts. Only the song title, BPM and a per-bar intensity summary are sent to it, never personal data, and there are daily usage limits.

\- Beat/BPM detection is classic audio analysis, not generative AI.

Process

\- I decide what the game should be: the modes, the rules, what feels right. The AI implements it, I play-test in VR, and I send back what feels wrong. It is a loop of design, implementation, playing and fixing.

\- Example 1: Dance mode charts were missing after a mode change. I only noticed because I was playing and recording footage in VR. The AI then traced it to a bug in how charts are converted when the mode switches.

\- Example 2: the AI sometimes breaks things in small ways. For instance, it once wrote string literals with wrong escape characters, and the compile check caught it. Automated compile checks and real play-testing are what keep this reliable.

\- Things like VR feel, difficulty, and how a mode plays can't be judged by the AI. Those are my calls.

What I do by hand

\- Game design and rules, VR play-testing, deciding priorities, store submissions and release work, and the final decision on every feature.

Happy to answer any questions about the workflow.
